unknowns_2026_11_16: PC version: no PC release or date appears in any official GTA VI material reviewed. Every Rockstar and Take-Two source lists PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only.
Map size: Rockstar has published no numeric map size or comparison with GTA V's map. Its wording is only 'sprawling state of Leonida' and 'biggest, most immersive evolution'.

Online / multiplayer: no GTA VI online mode has been officially detailed. The pre-order release calls it 'a single-player experience', and GTA+ is linked to GTA Online / GTA V, not to a confirmed GTA VI online mode.
UK pricing in GBP: only US prices ($79.99 Standard, $99.99 Ultimate) were seen in official material. UK store prices were not checked.
PEGI / UK age rating was not checked. Only ESRB M was seen on Rockstar's pages.

Gameplay systems (wildlife behaviour, in-game social media apps, character switching, properties, heists, police/wanted system changes) have not been officially described as gameplay features. Wildlife appears only in cover-art alt-text, and social media only in character bios.
Story length, mission count and number of playable characters: official copy names Jason and Lucia as leads but does not explicitly state the playable character count.
Frame rate options: Rockstar says it 'targets 30 frames per second'. No 60fps or performance mode on any console has been announced, and PS5 Pro details mention only PSSR and ray-traced shadows.
Physical disc: the June 2026 release describes the physical version as 'containing a download code inside the box' and does not confirm a playable disc.
Contents of 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival' (Newswire, 9 Nov 2026) and the full Album/Score track lists were not read.

Content rights: Rockstar's fan-content policy covers non-commercial use only. Any use of official trailers, screenshots, artwork or logos in a monetised or revenue-oriented TikTok needs a licence from copyright@take2games.com. No such permission is known to exist.
A '26 minutes gameplay' YouTube video appeared in endscreen links on the Rockstar videos page. It is not verified as official Rockstar material and should not be cited.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.topic: 1. Rockstar fan-content policy: what counts as non-commercial
platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: Rockstar Support's 'Policy on posting copyrighted Rockstar Games material' (last updated 10 January 2025) says: "Generally, Take-Two Interactive does not object to our fans using materials for non-commercial uses in a manner which does not intentionally spoil the plot for others." It defines the term this way: "'Non-commercial' means that you don't make money through the game footage you post or use the material as part of a promotion for a product or service. Take-Two Interactive reserves the right to have its copyrighted material taken down at any time." It also says: "this policy is intended to address occasional, non-commercial in-game content use by individual members of the Rockstar fan community."
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: Any monetised TikTok, including Creator Rewards and brand deals, falls outside what this policy tolerates if it contains Rockstar material. The safe route is 100% original motion graphics, our own narration and text. Mention facts only, and show no Rockstar footage, screenshots, artwork or logos. Even tolerated fan use can be taken down at any time.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.topic: 1b. Rockstar policy: pre-release footage, spoilers, in-game TV
platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: From the same page: "Pre-Release Footage: No pre-release leaked footage of any kind. Any posting of in-game footage from leaked copies of the game prior to its official release date will be taken down, regardless of how the game was obtained. This includes 'early unboxing' videos." On spoilers: "Posting video showing the ending of the game, an edited combination of cutscenes and/or in-game plot dialogue, or any other big reveal in the story... isolated videos of the game's cinematics will be removed." On in-game entertainment: "Showing content like the TV shows and comedy performances in Grand Theft Auto... any posting of these in isolation will be flagged for removal." Questions go to copyright@take2games.com.
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: For 16 to 18 November: no leaked clips, no early-unboxing posts and no 'leak' hooks. After launch on 19 November, the 'unusual details' series must not post isolated cutscenes, the ending or plot reveals, or clips of in-game TV and comedy shows. Narrated play-throughs are tolerated, but only on a non-commercial basis.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.topic: 2. Reuse of official GTA VI artwork, screenshots, logos and map
platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: rockstargames.com/VI/media/artwork-wallpapers offers '27 artwork and wallpapers (as zip file)', including 'Official Cover Art', 'Vice City Postcard' and versions 'With Logos'. A scrape asking for any terms of use or licence on that page returned none. The Newswire post of 3 November 2026 says: "On November 19 we will be adding an official printable Grand Theft Auto VI cover art poster and map of Leonida as a free digital download." The Newswire launch gallery post of 5 November 2026 points to rockstargames.com/VI/launch-gallery. Rockstar's legal terms (rockstargames.com/legal) say Rockstar owns all 'Content' ("designs, graphics, artwork, illustrations, photographs... characters, names... locations... trademarks, logos"). Section 2.2 is titled 'Personal, Non-Commercial Use Only'. Section 2.3 says you may not "copy... distribute... modify, create derivative works, commercialize, or otherwise exploit the Services (including the Content)... unless subject to separate, express written terms provided by Rockstar permitting such conduct." It also prohibits using Content to "develop, train, enhance, or provide source material for... any Generative AI Tools."
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: I found no grant allowing fan creators to reuse official screenshots, wallpapers, cover art, logos, trailer footage or the Leonida map in monetised posts. Being free to download does not make it licensed. Do not use these in videos or carousels, and do not trace them or feed them to AI image tools; the AI ban is explicit. The 'map dump' carousel idea needs original, stylised graphics, or written permission from copyright@take2games.com. Also note that the official map is only released on 19 November, so it does not exist yet on 16 November.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: TikTok Support ('How is AI-generated content labeled on TikTok?') says: "we encourage creators to label content that has been either completely generated or significantly edited by AI. We also require creators to label all AI-generated content that contains realistic images, audio, and video." TikTok's in-app AIGC page says: "While we encourage creators to disclose content that is completely AI-generated or significantly edited with AI, we require it for realistic images, audio, and video," and "TikTok may automatically apply the 'AI-generated' label to content that we identify as completely generated or significantly edited with AI." Note that support.tiktok.com would not scrape directly, so this text comes from the search excerpt of that page.
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: Synthetic text-to-speech that sounds like a realistic human voice counts as 'realistic audio', so turn on the AIGC label for every video that uses TTS narration. Do this even though the voice imitates no real person, and even when the visuals are non-AI motion graphics. Labelling is encouraged anyway, costs little, and avoids enforcement under the Integrity and Authenticity guidelines. Never clone a real person's voice. Note that Metricool's help page says its AI-generated content toggle works only for video posts, not photo posts.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: From TikTok For Business's blog post 'Video Scheduler': "You can find this feature on the web upload page. You can schedule videos anywhere from 15 minutes to 10 days in advance of publishing." Once a post is scheduled, "you cannot edit the video, caption, or scheduled time." The post also says: "You'll need a Business Account in order to access desktop scheduling," while elsewhere describing the feature as for 'creators and Business Accounts'. Buffer, a third party, claims 30 days, which conflicts with TikTok's own 10 days.
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: The 17 November videos (and any later 16 November slots) can be scheduled natively at tiktok.com/tiktokstudio/upload, at least 15 minutes ahead. Captions, the AIGC toggle and the time must be final before scheduling, because edits mean deleting the post and uploading again. If the Schedule option does not appear, the account may need to be a Creator or Business account.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.topic: 4b. Photo and carousel posts: desktop and music
platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: Metricool's help centre (updated 4 November 2026) says TikTok photo posts take JPEG or WebP, up to 20 MB per image, up to 1080p. "TikTok does not support PNG. The web version converts PNG files to JPG when you save the post. The mobile app does not convert them, so use JPG for TikTok photos in the app, or create the post on the web." On music: "Business accounts can add TikTok's Top 100 trending songs. Personal accounts can only add random music to photos." Sked Social (October 2026) says the API accepts "up to 35 images in a single photo post," and that "TikTok can add recommended music to photo posts automatically, but only when a tool uses direct post mode. If your carousel arrives in the TikTok inbox instead, add the sound yourself in the app." It also warns: "If your tool turns the images into an MP4 first, TikTok treats it as a video." TikTok For Business points businesses to the Commercial Music Library of pre-cleared tracks. I could not open an official TikTok page confirming native photo-post scheduling in TikTok Studio web, so treat that as unverified.
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: Export carousel slides as 1080x1920 JPG, not PNG. Native web scheduling is officially documented only for videos, so photo posts are safest published from the TikTok app, with sound added in-app. Business accounts are limited to Commercial Music Library or pre-cleared tracks. Personal accounts get the full music library for organic use, but those rights do not cover Creator Rewards or branded use. Original or royalty-free music baked into our own videos avoids muting.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.topic: 5. Content Posting API and third-party schedulers
platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: TikTok's developer Content Sharing Guidelines say: "Unaudited API Clients can only post contents in SELF_ONLY viewership. To make the contents publicly viewable later on, the account owner must first change their account visibility to public, and then change the privacy settings of each content to 'Everyone.'" The Direct Post reference adds: "All content posted by unaudited clients will be restricted to private viewing mode." Metricool's help centre says: "You can schedule and automatically publish your TikTok videos from Metricool for personal and business accounts... To publish automatically, the AUTO PUBLISH button must be enabled... carousel with up to 35 images is supported." Its auto-publish duration limit is 3 seconds to 10 minutes. It also says: "Choose manual publishing when you need features not available via the TikTok API, such as adding effects or music outside TikTok's Top 100 trending songs... At the scheduled time, Metricool sends you a notification to finish the post directly in the TikTok app." Sked Social notes that inbox/upload mode allows "at most five pending inbox shares in any 24 hours."
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: A home-made API app would only post private (SELF_ONLY) videos until TikTok audits it, so it is no use for this launch. Metricool documents public auto-publish for TikTok videos and carousels, which implies an audited integration, though I could not open TikTok's own list of approved partners. A Metricool MCP connector appears among this session's deferred tools. If @yourviral7 is connected to Metricool, its createScheduledPost tool is the legitimate scheduling route, with the user's explicit authorisation. Otherwise, use native TikTok Studio web scheduling.

platform_rules_2026_11_16.finding: TikTok Support ('Who is eligible to join the Creator Rewards Program?') says videos must "Be at least one minute long" and that "Video views must be longer than 5 seconds." It also says: "Videos under the program that contain copyrighted music for over one minute are at risk of being muted." TikTok Creator Academy says: "It must be original, high-quality content over 1 minute long." A third-party summary (creatorsagency.co) adds that eligible videos must be posted after enrolment, unsponsored and above 1,000 qualified For You views. That last point is not confirmed on an official page.
platform_rules_2026_11_16.implication_for_yourviral7: The 25 to 40 second prelaunch cuts will earn nothing from Creator Rewards. Only 65 to 90 second analytical versions can qualify, and only when the analysis justifies the length. Monetising also triggers Rockstar's 'commercial' line, so revenue-eligible videos must contain no Rockstar footage, art or logos, only original graphics and narration. Avoid copyrighted music in long cuts.
